value: bimodal activity peaks around dawn and dusk during all four seasons
method: 100 infrared cameras at 573 sites, 93,606 effective camera-trap days; independent detection = same species more than 30 min apart; activity from counts of independent detections per two-hour period (Daily Activity Index), read by visual inspection of the daily activity
conditions: Wild golden takin, Changqing National Nature Reserve, Shaanxi, China (107°25'-107°45'E, 33°26'-33°43'N; 299 km2; 800-3,000 m). n = 3,323 independent detections in total (from 12,351 detections); per season 1,088 spring, 1,169 autumn, 686 summer, 380 winter. Evening peak higher than the morning peak; lower activity 20:00-06:00, with a few animals moving 23:30-02:00. Peaks given by season: spring 06:00-08:00 and 18:00-20:00; autumn 06:00-08:00 and 16:00-18:00; summer 07:30-09:30 and 17:30-19:30; winter 07:30-09:30 and 15:30-17:30.

method: infrared camera traps; activity curves of independent photos by season; NRAI = night-time relative abundance index
conditions: Wild animals, Xianxialing Nature Reserve, Jiangshan, Zhejiang, China; 97 infrared cameras, January 2021 to November 2023, 71,879 effective camera-days; independent photo = consecutive records of one species at one camera within 30 min counted once. Diel activity by the night-time relative abundance index (NRAI; above 13/24 nocturnal, below diurnal) and activity curves by season. n = 236 independent photos of Tibetan Macaque (Table 1, column 'Number of independent photos'; relative abundance index 0.3283). Peak activity 12:00 h in summer and winter, 06:00-12:00 h in spring and autumn, secondary peak 18:00 h in spring. By the paper's species-order NRAI list (0.966, 0.922, 0.899, 0.545, 0.384, 0.381, 0.143, 0.042, 0.040) the Tibetan Macaque value is 0.042, below 13/24, which the paper reads as diurnal.

value: weak nocturnality (NRAI 0.545, close to the classification threshold)
method: infrared camera traps; NRAI = night-time relative abundance index, nocturnal when above 13/24
conditions: Wild animals, Xianxialing Nature Reserve, Jiangshan, Zhejiang, China; 97 infrared cameras, January 2021 to November 2023, 71,879 effective camera-days; independent photo = consecutive records of one species at one camera within 30 min counted once. Diel activity by the night-time relative abundance index (NRAI; above 13/24 nocturnal, below diurnal) and activity curves by season. n = 154 independent photos of Chinese Serow (Table 1; printed as Capricornis sumatraensis (Bechstein, 1799); relative abundance index 0.2142). The paper also says Chinese Serow showed an irregular activity pattern, peaking only around midnight in spring. NRAI 0.545 is above the 13/24 (0.542) nocturnal cut-off, which the paper calls close to the threshold.

method: camera traps, 493 stations and 102,879 camera-trap days (2012-2021); independent detection events = records of one species at one site more than 30 min apart; daily rhythms by kernel density estimation (R overlap package)
conditions: Wild alpine musk deer, Mt. Gongga, Sichuan, China. n = 109 valid activity detections retained for the kernel analysis (Section 3.3); Section 3.1 gives 112 independent effective detection events at 36 sites (2870-4572 m), so the two counts differ. The Results describe a bimodal pattern with peaks 08:00-10:00 and 19:00-21:00 and relatively lower nocturnal intensity; the Abstract calls the species primarily diurnal. Sympatric forest musk deer was mostly nocturnal (already on main).
